dedupe_keys.name: radioplanner 3 0 rf planning tool for mobile broadcast and private networks

description: RadioPlanner 3.0 is a desktop radio-frequency planning tool for mobile, private and broadcast networks. It covers 5G NR, LTE, UMTS, GSM and GSM-R mobile networks and fixed wireless access, public safety land mobile radio (P25, TETRA, DMR, dPMR and NXDN), IoT networks (LoRa, Sigfox, NB-IoT and LTE-M), terrestrial television and radio (ATSC 1.0 and 3.0, DVB-T and T2, ISDB-T, DTMB, DAB+, HD Radio and FM), and air-to-ground links for drones, ADS-B, VOR and DME. Propagation models include ITU-R P.1812-6, ITU-R P.1546-6, Longley-Rice ITM 1.2.2, Okumura-Hata, 3GPP TR 38.901 and a combined ITU-R P.528 and P.526 model for air-to-ground paths. It computes received power, best server, carrier to interference and noise ratio, throughput, coverage probability, LTE and 5G RSRP, EPRE and RSRQ, simulcast delay spread, talk-out and talk-back and field strength, and for broadcasters FCC and ITU-R P.1546 contours, population coverage and lists of localities covered, with frequency planning, path profiles and multipoint studies for customer premises or sensors. Coverage: worldwide use with terrain and clutter data. Format and access: commercial Windows software with a free trial and user manual. Caveats: proprietary; clutter and terrain inputs drive accuracy. Simulation uses: coverage and capacity planning of mobile, emergency and broadcast networks, and mapping coverage lost after site failures. Related records: Py1812 and Py1546 implement the same ITU-R methods openly, and the NTIA ITM model is the Longley-Rice reference.
